## New features & enhancements

- **The radio tells you which version it is now running.** The readout says `UPDATED TO V1.4.12` on the first launch after an update · six blinks, then your station. Never on a fresh install.
- Until now nothing said so: an update replaces the files under a closed radio, and the installer window is gone by the time you look.
- **The console theme strikes its cells whenever the name changes.** Each character holds what it says and flickers dark, dim, half-lit, lit, every cell on its own clock · the way a vacuum fluorescent display arrives at something new.
- **The installer closes the radio before it writes, and opens it again afterwards.** Windows will not move a folder a running browser sits in, which is what made the profile rename fail quietly.
- What it may close is narrow: a browser process whose own command line names this app's profile folder. Ordinary browsing is untouched.
- **The update pill arrives and leaves.** In over 220ms, out over 90ms on the cross. Its old 60ms fade was a snap: nothing was seen to happen.
- **One brighter alert orange**, in both places the mark appears and on every theme. At 5px it has to carry against walnut and near-black alike.
- **The installer names the version it is replacing**, reading it out of the copy already on disk rather than only out of a file that installs older than this one never shipped.
- **The Service tab carries the update dot too.** The mark on the Settings control says there is news somewhere in the drawer; this says which tab. And "New v… available" is written in the same orange, darkened until it can actually be read on a white ground.

## Bug fixes

- **A profile that cannot be renamed is used rather than abandoned.** If something still held the old folder, the launcher started an empty one instead · the radio came up with none of your stations.
- Nothing was ever actually lost, but nothing said so either.
